summary: Validate cross-account role chaining and remediate permission gaps for prod->analytics IAM bridge
description:
Issue summary:
We observed intermittent authorization failures when the prod inference service in the aws-main account attempts to assume the analytics-reader role in the gcp-analytics project via our federation bridge. Failures present as AccessDenied errors in the bridge logs and missing events in downstream analytics pipelines.

Impact:
- Analytics ingestion has sporadic gaps for ~3% of inference requests routed to analytics, causing skew in usage metrics and billing attribution.
- No user-facing outage, but metrics/reports used for billing and capacity planning are affected.

Environment:
- prod (aws-main account id: 111122223333) -> federation proxy -> gcp-analytics (project: redwood-analytics-prod)
- Bridge implemented via short-lived AWS STS -> GCP workload identity federation with a proxies service in k8s (cluster infra-proxy-prod).

Observed behavior:
- STS AssumeRole returns success, then proxy attempts to exchange credentials for GCP identity and receives HTTP 403 / IAM_PERMISSION_DENIED from IAM token exchange endpoint.
- CloudTrail shows successful AssumeRole calls from the proxy service but the token-exchange step to GCP fails in same minute windows.
- Errors appear concentrated in us-east-1, with a smaller spike in us-west1.

Expected behavior:
- Seamless role chaining with sub-second token exchange success and no authorization errors.

Steps to reproduce / replication steps:
1) Trigger a synthetic inference workload from prod that routes telemetry to analytics (use synthetic job id SNY-permcheck-2026).
2) Tail infra-proxy-prod logs in namespace infra-proxy-prod: kubectl logs -f deploy/proxy --since=10m.
3) Monitor CloudTrail AssumeRole logs for caller arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/proxy-role/* and check GCP token exchange endpoint logs (token-exchange.googleapis.com).
4) Observe 403 errors on token-exchange and correlate with STS success entries.

Logs / Evidence:
- infra-proxy-prod logs snippet (Mar 10 03:14 UTC): "ERROR token-exchange: failed to exchange aws-session for gcp-identity: status=403 detail=Permission denied: serviceAccountTokenCreator missing"
- CloudTrail (Mar 10 03:14 UTC): AssumeRole succeeded for principal: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/proxy-role
- GCP audit (redwood-analytics-prod): "MethodName=GenerateAccessToken Resource=serviceAccount:redwood-analytics-sa@redwood-analytics-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com Response=PERMISSION_DENIED"

Additional notes:
- This pattern started around 2026-03-08 after the infra team rotated a subset of service account bindings and tightened a set of IAM conditions for serviceAccountTokenCreator on the analytics service account.
- The issue is intermittent; many exchanges succeed while others get PERMISSION_DENIED. Hypothesis: a policy condition tied to "request.time" or tag propagation may intermittently not be present on short-lived session credentials.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypotheses and checks performed:
- Hypothesis 1: Role chaining works but GCP service account binding condition rejects some sessions. Checked GCP IAM binding history and found a recent addition of a conditional binding requiring attribute 'aws:principalTag/env=prod'.
- Hypothesis 2: Tag propagation from AWS STS -> proxy -> GCP token exchange is missing for some requests because proxy does not forward session tags. Confirmed proxy code path only attaches tags when NewSession field set; synthetic tests showed missing tags in failing traces.
- Performed deterministic replay with synthetic session that included aws:sts:session-tag env=prod and saw token-exchange succeed 100% of the time.
- Correlated logs: failing traces consistently lacked session metadata header X-AWS-Session-Tags.
- Checked ks-config for infra-proxy-prod: older deployment revision (v2026.02.18) does not include the session-tag middleware; new revision (v2026.03.05) includes it but rollout partial (50%).
- Risk assessment: partial rollout plus conditional IAM bindings explains intermittent nature.
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4721 (adds session-tag passthrough).
comments: Arjun Patel (2026-03-10): Filed initial ticket after noticing analytics gaps; posted summary to #infra-support with links to CloudTrail and GCP audit logs.
Lena Morales (2026-03-10): Assigned for remediation. Plan: verify proxy rollout state and confirm whether we need to rollback the conditional IAM or complete the proxy rollout.

Infra Oncall (Rami Durand) (2026-03-11): Checked k8s rollout: infra-proxy-prod at revision v2026.03.05 at 50% healthy. Node selector mismatch caused half of pods to remain on older revision. Opening hotfix rollout.
Security (Priya Kaur) (2026-03-11): Conditional IAM binding was applied intentionally to reduce blast radius. We prefer fixing proxy to preserve security posture rather than reverting IAM change.

Lena Morales (2026-03-12): Completed hot rollout to 100% of infra-proxy-prod with v2026.03.05. Monitoring shows successful token-exchange rate increased from ~97% to ~99.99% in last 12 hours. Continuing observation window 24h.
Arjun Patel (2026-03-12): Noted downstream analytics backfill job scheduled to reconcile missing events; ETA for full reconciliation 2026-03-15.
resolution:
Partial remediation completed (2026-03-12):
- Deployed infra-proxy-prod v2026.03.05 to 100%, which includes session-tag passthrough middleware. This addresses the missing X-AWS-Session-Tags header that caused GCP conditional IAM bindings to reject some exchanges.
- No rollback of GCP conditional IAM performed; security team prefers this posture.
- Observed success rate for token exchanges improved to ~99.99%.
- Follow-ups:
  1) Run reconciliation backfill job for analytics (task assigned to analytics team, job id: ANL-FILL-2026-03-12).
  2) Add synthetic end-to-end regression to infra CI to validate session-tag passthrough on every proxy deploy (infra ticket INT-200101 created).
  3) Update runbook in Confluence with troubleshooting steps and common error signatures.
- Status: Monitoring (will close once backfill confirmed and 48h of stable telemetry observed).
workaround: Until proxy rollout completed, temporarily add an exception for the conditional IAM by allowing the token-exchange principal (proxy-role) an unconditional serviceAccountTokenCreator permission. This was considered but rejected by Security; prefer completing proxy rollout.
next_steps:
1) Verify analytics backfill completes and confirm metrics aligned (owner: Analytics Team).
2) Add synthetic regression to CI and gate proxy deployments on tag passthrough tests (owner: Infra).
3) Close ticket after 48h stable observation and successful backfill.
4) Postmortem to capture rollout process gap and add guardrail to k8s rollout automation to avoid partial revision stuck on node selectors.
notes:
Key observables: CloudTrail AssumeRole entries, infra-proxy logs for X-AWS-Session-Tags header presence, GCP IAM audit for GenerateAccessToken PERMISSION_DENIED.
Escalation path: #infra-support -> oncall -> secops if permission changes requested.
